record.original_question: If an F-division algebra has prime period, must it be a crossed product? In other words, for each prime p, is every central division algebra whose Brauer class has order p necessarily obtained from a Galois crossed-product construction?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Determine whether F-division algebras of prime period are crossed products.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $D$ be a central division algebra over $F$, i.e., a finite-dimensional associative $F$-algebra with center exactly $F$ in which every nonzero element is invertible. The period (or exponent) of $D$ is the order of its class $[D]$ in the Brauer group $\mathrm{Br}(F)$. The algebra $D$ is called a crossed product if it contains a maximal subfield $K \subset D$ such that $K/F$ is a Galois extension; equivalently, $D \cong (K/F, G, c)$ for some Galois group $G = \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ and some 2-cocycle $c \in Z^2(G, K^\times)$.

Question: For every prime number $p$, every field $F$, and every central $F$-division algebra $D$ whose period in $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ equals $p$, must $D$ be a crossed product?
artifact.category_tag: Central simple algebras and crossed products
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether central division algebras of prime period must be crossed products is widely regarded as open. While Amitsur (1972) constructed noncrossed products in general, no noncrossed product of prime period (or prime degree, for odd primes) is known, and no proof that such algebras are always crossed products exists. Recent literature (e.g., work on noncyclic division algebras of prime degree) continues to treat this as an outstanding open question.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on central simple algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 2.1. Determine whether F-division algebras of prime period are crossed products.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Non cyclic division algebras of prime degree
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work produces examples of division algebras of prime degree that are not cyclic, while the crossed-product question for prime period/degree remains open.
status_evidence.claim: No noncrossed products of prime period are known; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: A note on Amitsur's noncrossed product theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Amitsur's noncrossed product construction and the absence of prime-period examples.
status_evidence.claim: Noncrossed products exist in general (Amitsur 1972) but not at prime period.
